title: Indian Statutory Commission Simon Commission 1927
definition: A seven-member all-British commission appointed by the British Conservative government under Sir John Simon to report on the working of the Government of India Act 1919 and suggest further constitutional reforms.
importanceInUpsc: It serves as a critical turning point in the Indian National Movement, marking the transition from moderate constitutional agitation to mass-based radical nationalism and the demand for Purna Swaraj.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Indian Statutory Commission Simon Commission 1927.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
